sites.functional_impact_measured: L11: KCC2-FLAG surface labeling confirmed by non-permeabilized immunostaining in neurons; L8: FLAG antibody signal used as surface-display readout for 96 KCC2 mutants. No ion-transport functional assay specifically for the EL3-FLAG construct is reported.
sites.rationale: The rat KCC2b (1116 aa) position 383–384 cited in L1 falls within EL3 of that ortholog. The human canonical sequence (1139 aa, KCC2a isoform) has 23 extra N-terminal residues, so the orthologous junction maps to human position 406–407 (T406|P407), computed by adding the 23-aa isoform offset. Position 406 lies within human EL3 (303–418), 104 residues from the TM5 C-terminus (302) and 13 residues from TM6 (419), satisfying the ≥3-residue TM-distance constraint. The cited_tag_residue is 383 (rat KCC2b); the human position 406 is inferred. L1 describes this as a 'low-conserved region', consistent with tolerance of an insertion. L1 reports a FLAG tag inserted 'between amino acid positions 383 and 384 of the rat KCC2b' (NM_134363.1, 1116 aa) in the 'low-conserved region of the 3rd extracellular loop'. The human canonical SLC12A5 sequence (1139 aa) is the KCC2a isoform, which carries 23 additional N-terminal residues relative to KCC2b; the human equivalent of rat KCC2b position 383 is therefore 383 + 23 = 406. L11 confirms surface accessibility of the FLAG tag in this loop by non-permeabilized immunostaining of transfected neurons. L8 uses the same FLAG-EL3 construct as a surface-display reporter to screen C-terminal transposon mutants.

sources.claim: The extracellular FLAG-tag was inserted into the low-conserved region of the 3rd extracellular loop between amino acid positions 383 and 384 of the rat KCC2b.

sites.rationale: [Literature audit 2026-11-05 (deliverome-analysis PR 236), verdict confirmed_shifted: insert_after_residue NULL -> 248: the paper pins the junction on human canonical Q9H2X9 (paper numbering: ortholog:mouse (KCC2b, NM_020333), construct species: mouse). validation_level surface_and_function -> function_only (paper reports surface: not_reported, function: yes). Paper (PMID 34019872): "we used KCC2b with a 3xHA tag (IFYPYDVPDYAGYPYDVPDYAG-SYPYDVPDYAAHAAA) in EL2 of the KCC2b clone (KCC2bHA). The tag with a length of 37 amino acid residues is inserted at the end of EL2 reaching into TM4 (31) (Fig. 1A). ... We included the 3xHA tag between Ala225 and Met226.". Audit note: Recoverable: the Ala225|Met226 pair (stated for the homology models built of the KCC2bHA construct) is mouse KCC2b numbering (NP_065066: FKAEDASGEAAA225|M226LNNMRVYGTCV); human canonical Q9H2X9 (KCC2a-type N-terminus) has the identical context at A248|M249, the same +23 isoform offset verified for training row SLC12A5-406, so insert_after = 248, at the end of EL2 (human 231-253) before TM4. The construct itself is from Zhao et al. 2008 Cell Signal (ref 31); mouse KCC2b with 3xHA only (no pHluorin or 3xFLAG in this paper). Function: Tl+ flux of KCC2bHA 'indistinguishable from KCC2bWT' in HEK-293. Surface: no surface assay in this paper.] EL2 of human SLC12A5 spans residues 231–253 (23 aa), flanked by TM3 (ends 230) and TM4 (starts 254). At least nine independent publications insert 3xHA, pHluorin, or 3xFLAG tags into this loop in full-length, membrane-anchored KCC2b constructs and confirm surface display; L6 explicitly states biochemical properties are preserved. No paper names a specific junction residue within EL2, so the site is reported at region level. The loop is 23 aa long and fully extracellular, providing ample space for a short epitope tag. Multiple full-length, membrane-anchored KCC2b constructs (rat and mouse) carry 3xHA, pHluorin, or 3xFLAG tags inserted into the second extracellular loop (EL2) of the full-length transporter expressed in heterologous cells and neurons. L12 is the most positionally specific, stating the 37-aa 3xHA tag is 'inserted at the end of EL2 reaching into TM4'. L6 reports that pHluorin insertion in the extracellular loop 'did not disturb the biochemical properties of the proteins compared to their nontagged homologs'. L15 confirms surface display by non-permeabilized anti-FLAG staining.
